transcript.content: Hello, I'm glad you're here today. What brings you in to see me?

My mind just never shuts off—I feel like I can’t stop worrying about school and everything I’m responsible for, no matter what I do. It’s gotten to the point where I just can't seem to shake it off anymore.
How long have you been experiencing this constant worry, and did it start after a specific stressful event or change in your life?

This has been going on for about seven months now. It started shortly after my school district introduced a major curriculum overhaul and a new data-driven evaluation system. The massive increase in workload and the pressure to track all these new metrics really seemed to trigger this constant worry.
Along with this constant worry, have you also been feeling down, sad, or losing interest in things you normally enjoy?

Yes, I’ve definitely lost the enjoyment I used to get from my hobbies because I'm just so exhausted. By the end of the day, I'm too drained to do anything other than sit on the couch and stare at the TV. It has forced me to neglect the things I love, like working on the robotics club designs, community theater, and even tossing a baseball with my son.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about other areas of your life, like your family, health, or minor daily tasks, or is the worry mostly focused on your schoolwork?

It definitely started with school, but now it has spread to other areas of my life. My mind constantly jumps from worrying about lesson plans and test scores to whether I'm screwing up our finances or being a bad husband and dad. It all feels completely blown out of proportion, but I just can't seem to stop the thoughts.
Along with this constant worry, have you been experiencing physical symptoms like muscle tension, feeling restless or on edge, or having trouble sleeping?

Yes, I constantly feel revved up like I've had too much coffee, and my neck and shoulders get so tight that I get dull headaches from clenching my jaw. Even when I manage to get to bed at a reasonable hour, I still wake up completely exhausted and just drag myself through the day.
Besides feeling exhausted and worried, have you also been experiencing a persistent sad, low, or empty mood most of the day, nearly every day?
No, I wouldn't say I feel sad or empty in that way. It's more that my mind is constantly racing with anxiety and worry, and my body just feels incredibly tense and keyed up all the time.
Have you noticed if this constant worry makes you feel more irritable or easily annoyed with others, or does it cause you to have trouble concentrating on your tasks?

Yes, unfortunately, both have been a real problem. I've found myself losing my patience and snapping at my wife and son at home, which I feel terrible about. At school, I'm so preoccupied that I've been missing details in my lesson plans and procrastinating, and my principal even pointed out that I seemed scattered in meetings.

Major depressive disorder has been ruled out as the primary driver. Therefore, F41.1 remains the sole candidate, and the diagnosis is final.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets the diagnostic criteria for Generalized Anxiety Disorder (ICD-10: F41.1). He reports excessive, uncontrollable anxiety and worry about multiple areas of life (schoolwork, finances, family roles) for approximately seven months. This worry is accompanied by multiple physical and cognitive symptoms, including feeling keyed up or on edge, muscle tension (neck/shoulder tightness and jaw clenching), irritability, difficulty concentrating (scatteredness and procrastination at work), and sleep disturbance (waking up unrefreshed). These symptoms cause significant functional impairment across occupational, social, and familial domains.
